name: sidebar

frames.best_why: Rail is fully open with every icon labelled beside it and the content panel visible.

tagline: Narrow icon rail widens on hover to reveal menu names.
summary: A dark left-hand navigation strip of icons that expands into a wider panel with labels when hovered, easing back to icons alone. It sits beside the page content.
appearance: A narrow dark grey rail pinned to the left of a bordered panel, holding five small line icons in a vertical stack. Expanded, it widens into a slab and each icon gains a small grey label; the rest of the panel reads 'Main content area'.
behaviour: Hovering the rail slides it open to show labels and pushes the content area aside; moving away shrinks it back to the icon strip. The width eases rather than snapping.
demo_content: Five links named Home, Dashboard, Documents, Profile and Settings; the body reads 'Main content area'.
search_phrases: collapsible icon rail that opens on hover
app nav with labels on hover
left menu strip with small icons
icon rail beside the main content
use_when: A dashboard needs to save width but still let people read the menu labels on demand.
avoid_when: Labels only appear on hover, so touch users see icons alone, and the width jump reflows the page.
customise: Compose Sidebar, SidebarBody and SidebarLink with your own link objects, and control open state through Sidebar props. Widths, hover behaviour and colours are fixed in the file.
weight_why: A handful of links and one width animation; no loops or heavy assets.

a11y.note: Collapsed links hide their text with display:none, leaving icon-only anchors unnamed, and the width change ignores reduced-motion.

issues: Collapsed links show icons only, with their text hidden and no accessible name.
The content area jumps sideways as the rail opens and closes.
polish_why: Tidy icon rail and smooth width change; it is plain and the hover-only labels are limiting.
title: Sidebar
